message.content: The court may grant summary judgment where a party has no real prospect of success on the claim or issue, and there is no other compelling reason for a trial [Part 24 - Summary judgment]. The costs of proceedings are governed by Practice Direction 44, which gives the court discretion over whether costs are payable, their amount, and timing [Practice Direction 44 - General rules about costs]. Before issuing proceedings, parties must comply with the relevant pre-action protocol; failure to do so may result in costs sanctions [Practice Direction - Pre-Action Conduct and Protocols]. In the Commercial Court, case management conferences are used to review issues and give directions up to trial [The Commercial Court Guide].

text.content: The court may give summary judgment against a claimant or defendant on the whole of a claim or on an issue if it considers that the claimant has no real prospect of succeeding on the claim or issue or the defendant has no real prospect of successfully defending the claim or issue and in either case there is no other compelling reason why the case or issue should be disposed of at a trial.
text.full_content:
PART 24 - SUMMARY JUDGMENT

24.2 The court may give summary judgment against a claimant or defendant on the whole of a claim or on an issue if (a) it considers that the claimant has no real prospect of succeeding on the claim or issue; or (b) the defendant has no real prospect of successfully defending the claim or issue; and (c) in either case, there is no other compelling reason why the case or issue should be disposed of at a trial.

24.3 The court may give summary judgment against a claimant in any type of proceedings.

24.4 Proceedings against the Crown may be the subject of an application under this Part.
text.category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

text.citation: 1.1, PD44, Practice Direction 44 - General rules about costs
text.content: This Practice Direction supplements Part 44. The court has discretion as to whether costs are payable by one party to another, the amount of those costs and when they are to be paid.
text.full_content:
PRACTICE DIRECTION 44 - GENERAL RULES ABOUT COSTS

1.1 This Practice Direction supplements Part 44. The court has discretion as to whether costs are payable by one party to another, the amount of those costs and when they are to be paid.

1.2 Where the court makes an order for costs, it may make a summary or detailed assessment of costs.

1.3 The general rule is that the unsuccessful party will be ordered to pay the costs of the successful party.

text.content: Before commencing proceedings, the court will expect the parties to have complied with this Practice Direction or the relevant pre-action protocol. If proceedings are issued, the parties may be required to provide evidence that alternative means of resolving their dispute were considered. The court may impose costs sanctions where a party has unreasonably failed to comply.
text.full_content:
PRACTICE DIRECTION - PRE-ACTION CONDUCT AND PROTOCOLS

4. Before commencing proceedings, the court will expect the parties to have complied with this Practice Direction or the relevant pre-action protocol. If proceedings are issued, the parties may be required to provide evidence that alternative means of resolving their dispute were considered. The court may impose costs sanctions where a party has unreasonably failed to comply.

5. The objectives of pre-action conduct are to enable parties to settle the issue between them without the need to start proceedings.

text.citation: D5.3, The Commercial Court Guide, The Commercial Court Guide
text.content: A case management conference will normally be fixed for a date shortly after the date for filing and service of the defence. At the case management conference the court will review the issues and the estimated length of the trial and give directions designed to assist in managing the case up to trial.
text.full_content:
THE COMMERCIAL COURT GUIDE

D5.3 A case management conference will normally be fixed for a date shortly after the date for filing and service of the defence. At the case management conference the court will review the issues and the estimated length of the trial and give directions designed to assist in managing the case up to trial.

D5.4 The parties should ensure that whoever attends the case management conference is familiar with the case and has authority to agree directions.
